title: Multi-Query Attention: Faster Decoding
hook: Share one key/value head across all query heads - the KV cache shrinks by a factor of H and decoding gets dramatically faster with barely any quality cost.
key_points: Replaces H independent key/value heads with a single shared KV head while keeping H query heads.
KV cache size drops by a factor of H, cutting memory bandwidth demand at each decoding step.
Autoregressive decoding is often memory-bandwidth-bound, so smaller KV = directly faster generation.
Proposed by Shazeer in 2019; later generalized by Grouped-Query Attention.
content_html: In 2019 Noam Shazeer (then at Google Brain) published a short but influential paper showing that most of the cost of multi-head attention during inference comes from loading keys and values from memory, not from compute. His fix was simple: keep multiple query heads but collapse all key and value projections down to a single shared head, cutting the KV cache by the number of heads.
extra_html:
How it works

Standard multi-head attention projects inputs into H separate query, key, and value matrices. Multi-query attention keeps all H query projections but uses only one key projection and one value projection, shared across every query head. At each decoding step the model must load the entire KV cache; with one KV head instead of H, that memory read shrinks by a factor of H. Compute per head is unchanged; only the memory footprint is reduced.

Why it matters

For autoregressive text generation, each new token requires attending to every prior token, which means repeatedly loading a growing KV cache from GPU memory. Shazeer showed this is the binding bottleneck at inference time. Multi-query attention directly addresses it, enabling faster generation and larger effective batch sizes. Grouped-query attention later softened the quality trade-off by allowing multiple shared KV heads. Read the original note on arXiv.

related.title: Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)
related.hook: Split the difference between multi-head and multi-query attention: share KV heads across groups of query heads and get most of the memory savings with little quality loss.

related.title: PagedAttention / vLLM: Efficient LLM Serving
related.hook: LLM serving wastes huge amounts of GPU memory on the attention cache. PagedAttention borrows an OS trick — paging — to recover it and serve many more requests at once.

related.title: The KV Cache & Continuous Batching
related.hook: Generating one token reuses every prior key and value - that growing cache is why LLM inference is memory-bound, and continuous batching is how servers fight back.

flashcards.prompt: Why does shrinking the KV cache speed up decoding?

choices.text: Decoding is memory-bandwidth-bound, so loading a smaller cache is faster
It reduces the compute per attention head
It removes the need to attend to prior tokens
